beats.say: This is what changed in RISE this week. Almost all of it is RISE Live.

RISE Live's face, Sophia, now holds every visual in one of three frames: the inner eye, the outer shell, and the full frame. The visual chooses the frame, and Sophia no longer leaves the room while a reading speaks.
A change of visual within a frame is one blink of the aperture. Under reduced motion, every change is instant and nothing blinks.
The ask bar now sits at the foot of the room, above the instrument and any on-screen keyboard, with the spoken words above it. That was the owner's decision.
In the full frame, a figure or a generated scene is now fitted clear of the ask bar and the words. Before, the demo's horizon figure put its own label under the progress line, clipped.
And Live now draws the circle frames at the size they are shown, so the harmonograph is no longer soft on a phone.

RISE Live also remembers the room. Each new question goes up with the earlier questions and what RISE said, so a follow-up such as: what did Einstein say about it? can be understood. It lives in the page's memory only; leaving the room or reloading forgets it.
A follow-up fixed how that memory names scenes, so a picture is no longer counted twice, and an answer's scene keeps the name the answer gave it.
During a reading, a reader who names one of RISE's own visuals now gets it at once, with no model call, and nothing is counted as usage.
That visual now also reaches the screen at once, instead of waiting for the next phrase. On one measured run, the wait had been 12 seconds.

Two visuals the owner kept from the Sophia design study became engine options. The attractor can be a swarm of seven hundred particles, and the harmonograph can be rotary, two pendulums turning opposite ways.
The swarm was slow in the venue, at 4 to 16 frames a second. It now adds each tick to its trail in one draw, and the flash gate samples on the GPU.
For the team: a browser test that failed from run to run was traced to a race. A choice panel opened while the page faded in was hidden when the question field took focus. Now it stays open.
That is the week in RISE.
